content: Moles are skin growths that occur when melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells in the skin, grow together in a cluster along with surrounding tissue. They are extremely common, with most individuals having between 10 and 40 moles on their body. New moles can develop periodically, typically up until the age of 40. Moles are generally pink, tan, or brown in color. They may appear either flat or raised and are usually round or oval in shape. Their size is typically no larger than the diameter of a pencil eraser. Approximately 10% of people have at least one atypical mole, which is medically referred to as a dysplastic nevus. These atypical moles differ in appearance from ordinary moles and may carry a higher risk of transforming into melanoma, a serious form of skin cancer. It is important to consult a healthcare professional if a mole appears unusual, increases in size, changes in color or shape, or exhibits any other concerning characteristics.
